# Pandamonium v1.0.53

This release makes the agent's work visible while it happens and fixes a subtle update-lifecycle regression. A collapsible todo panel now docks above the composer and follows the agent's own plan through a multi-step task, and an installed update is guaranteed to reload the page onto the new build even when the service worker cannot reconcile during the restart.

## MAD-917 — UI: docked collapsible agent todos/progress panel above the composer

### Problem

The agent already had an `update_plan` tool and streamed `plan_update` events with a markdown checklist, but the frontend that displayed them was removed with the old plan-mode code — leaving a dangling `_setStoredPlan` call and no visible progress. The agent's plan was invisible to the operator.

### Implementation

A new `static/js/agentPlan.js` parses the checklist (`- [x]` / `- [ ]` with nesting depth), renders a panel docked directly above the composer with an `N of M todos completed` header, done checkmarks with strikethrough, nested indentation, and the current step, and stores the latest plan per session. `chat.js` routes `plan_update` events into the module, the collapse chevron persists its state, session rendering restores the matching plan, and the panel stays hidden when a session has no plan. The `update_plan` tool description and agent cheat-sheet now present it as a general multi-step progress list rather than an approved-plan-only marker.

### Product value and UI visibility

While the agent works, the operator sees exactly what it intends to do, what is done, and what is next — updated live and collapsible when screen space matters. This is the agent's working list; the user-facing Tasks feature is untouched.

### Verification

`tests/test_agent_plan_panel.py` guards the markup, module contract, storage keys, chat wiring, and agent-facing wording. `tests/browser/agent-plan.spec.js` covers the live update, progress count, done/active/nested classes, collapse persistence across reload, and per-session isolation.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Frontend-only plus wording; the existing `plan_update` SSE contract is unchanged. Plans are stored per session in local browser storage, so they are device-local; no schema or API change. No new dependency.

### References

- [Linear MAD-917](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-917/ui-docked-collapsible-agent-todosprogress-panel-above-the-composer)
- [Feature PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/135)

## MAD-918 — Updater: restore automatic page refresh after an installed update

### Problem

After an update finished, the app stopped reloading itself onto the new release's assets. The page waited for the replacement service worker to activate and then returned, delegating the refresh entirely to the worker's own client reconcile. That reconcile only navigates windows when it can read a terminal update status during the restart window; when the read misses, nothing navigates and the operator keeps seeing the previous build until a manual refresh. The pending-marker fallback page could also load before the new worker was in control and was then only acknowledged, never refreshed.

### Implementation

`refreshApplicationWorker()` now reloads the page directly if the replacement worker activates but does not navigate this client within a bounded grace window (`WORKER_RECONCILE_FALLBACK_MS`). When the worker confirms an install to a page that took the pending fallback load, that page refreshes once so it renders the new build. The reconcile marker is removed before any refresh, so the fallback cannot loop, and reload only follows a successful update.

### Product value and UI visibility

An installed update reliably ends with the app showing the new release, closing the gap where a successful update could leave stale UI on screen.

### Verification

`tests/browser/updater.spec.js` passes 19/19, including a regression where the served replacement worker activates but never navigates: the page still reloads without any manual refresh. The existing signed-restart, stale-response, offline, rollback, and authorization updater scenarios were rerun unchanged.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Frontend-only change; the updater contract, rollback behavior, and failure paths are unchanged, and `updater.js` remains embeddable by the release-bridge harness. No new dependency.

### References

- [Linear MAD-918](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-918/updater-restore-automatic-page-refresh-after-an-installed-update)
- [Fix PR](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/139)
